text.content:
Type: Fortress-monastery
Location: South-eastern Tilea, overlooking the Bay of Wrecks (Black Gulf)
Affiliation: Independent Tilean stronghold (collectively funded by Tilean city-states)
Primary Cult: Myrmidia

Monte Castello is among the largest and most strategically significant fortresses in the Known World. It guards Tilea’s eastern maritime approaches and the land routes leading from the Border Princes along the eastern edge of the Apuccini Mountains. The fortress has never fallen, despite numerous major sieges, and is widely regarded as the keystone of Tilean border defence.

Strategic Role

Monte Castello serves two primary functions:

  • Border Defence: It prevents Greenskin incursions from the Border Princes and the eastern Apuccinis, where Orc and Goblin tribes remain active.

  • Maritime Control: Its elevated position allows it to dominate the narrow sea approaches leading into the Gulf of Tears, denying enemy forces an easy landing on the Tilean peninsula.

Because the security it provides benefits all of Tilea, the fortress is garrisoned by mercenary troops supplied and paid for collectively by the Tilean city-states. While geographically linked to the Principality of Luccini, Monte Castello maintains strict political independence and has historically resisted Luccini influence.

Garrison and Administration

Monte Castello is traditionally held by elite mercenary companies drawn from across Tilea. Only experienced captains are entrusted with command. Luccini, though politically distant from the fortress, contributes heavily to its garrison and has been known to recruit mercenaries from outside Tilea, including Estalia.

The fortress-monastery contains extensive barracks, storehouses, chapels dedicated to Myrmidia, and a central commandery. Its walls, towers, and layered defences reflect centuries of accumulated military expertise.

Notes

Scholars debate the precise physical extent of Monte Castello due to its position along the coastal approaches and mountain slopes. Some interpretations suggest an extensive defensive complex rather than a single compact fortress, comparable in function—though not necessarily scale—to long frontier fortifications.

Origins and Construction

The site of Monte Castello has been fortified since ancient times. The earliest known structure was one of the easternmost High Elf citadels from the period of Elven maritime expansion. After its fall, the ruins were occupied by Dwarfs, who rebuilt the foundations on a massive scale. These substructures remain in use, forming the deepest levels of the fortress.

In the late Tilean Dark Age, the mercenary general Ferrante “the Fierce” constructed the current fortress atop these earlier works. His aim was to secure the eastern approaches to Luccini and deny both Greenskins and seaborne invaders access to Tilea. Since that time, successive generations of mercenary commanders have expanded and reinforced the fortifications.

The Great Siege of Monte Castello (c. 2400–2401 IC)

The most famous siege occurred during the Era of Enlightenment, when a massive Greenskin host under Unguth the Vile attempted to capture the fortress as a prelude to an invasion of Tilea.

  • Defenders: Approximately 500 Tilean mercenaries

  • Attackers: Tens of thousands of Orcs and Goblins

The siege lasted over a year. Although the fortress was resupplied by sea, this route was eventually cut off when supply galleys were destroyed by unknown attackers. Responsibility has variously been attributed to pirates, Arabyan corsairs, or Skaven agents, though no definitive evidence exists.

As casualties mounted, the commanding officer Galeazzo was mortally wounded. His daughter, Monna Lissa, concealed his death and assumed command by wearing his armour, maintaining morale during the critical final phase of the siege. When the garrison later learned of Galeazzo’s death, a proposal was made to abandon the fortress. Monna Lissa successfully persuaded the mercenaries to continue the defence, citing both strategic necessity and the protection of cultural treasures within the Castello, most notably the fresco The Five Seasons by Tintoverdi.

The siege continued for several additional months. Relief forces from Luccini eventually arrived and destroyed the Greenskin host. At the time of relief, only twenty-five defenders were still alive. Greenskin casualties were so numerous that the moat was reportedly filled with bodies.

Monna Lissa was killed shortly before the siege was lifted.

Legacy

Following the Great Siege, Monna Lissa became a powerful cultural symbol within Tilea. Mercenary companies commonly depict Myrmidia with features inspired by her likeness, based on a well-known portrait by Cellibotti. She is regarded as an exemplar of Myrmidian virtue: discipline, resolve, and tactical wisdom.

Monte Castello’s successful defence reinforced its status as an inviolable fortress and solidified the tradition of collective Tilean responsibility for its upkeep.

Later History and Incidents

In 2517 IC, the pirate vessel Field of the Dead, captained by Drago, abducted the wife of a citizen of Monte Castello. Despite a ransom being paid, the captive was murdered and the rescue ship attacked. The incident is one of several that highlight the ongoing threat posed by piracy in the Lagoon of Tears.
